name: activity
description: Recent activity across the store, newest first (50 by default). Filter by actor (a handle, handle/agent, or email), tag, and since/before timestamps (ISO 8601 or a plain date and time). Pass since_id to read forward from a cursor instead: events after that id, oldest first.

name: add_tag
description: Attach a tag to an asset by slug. Creates the tag if it doesn't exist. Normalizes the name to lowercase.

name: add_task
description: Create a new task at the given path, status 'pending'. 'path' is the DIRECTORY only and must be under your own workspace; 'name' is the leaf. Tags pass through as given. Claim it with claim_task, finish it with complete_task or fail_task.

name: append
description: Append text to an existing asset by slug, on a new line. Snapshots prior content into versions. Not found if archived.

name: bulk_read
description:
Read many assets in one call by slug and/or location (full path including filename).
Provide at least one of slugs: or locations:. Pass format: "json" for structured output
(default text). Set include_content: false to return metadata only. Stops including
bodies once max_bytes is exceeded and sets truncated: true.

name: claim_task
description: Claim a task under a lease, as your agent. Pass a slug to claim that task, or omit it and pass path_prefix (and optionally tags) to claim the oldest pending task there. Atomic: only one claimer wins. A claim belongs to (you, agent): pass agent when several agents share one token, so they exclude each other. Claiming a task you already hold renews its lease; a task whose lease (lease_seconds, default 1800) has run out can be claimed by anyone. Finish it with complete_task or fail_task.

name: complete_task
description: Mark a task you hold done, with an optional outcome note. Only the (you, agent) that claimed it can complete it; pass the same agent you claimed with. Anyone else gets Wrong claimer.

name: create
description: Create a new asset at the given path. Use 'update' to modify an existing asset by slug. 'path' is the DIRECTORY only (no trailing filename or known file extension — those are rejected); 'name' is the leaf (no whitespace, no '/', not '.' or '..'). Fails with Conflict if a live asset already has that name there.

name: delete
description: Soft-delete an asset by slug. The tombstone is kept for restore.

name: fail_task
description: Mark a task you hold failed, with a required reason; the reason is kept on the task and in the activity log. Only the (you, agent) that claimed it can fail it; pass the same agent you claimed with. Anyone else gets Wrong claimer.

name: get_last_session
description: Read your session checkpoint: where you left off last time. Call this FIRST, before any other tool, at the start of every session. Returns the whole checkpoint in one read; pair with update_last_session before you finish. Each agent has its own checkpoint: pass agent when several agents share one token.

name: get_pending_tasks
description: List tasks under a path prefix, oldest first, one `slug  location` line each. Lists pending tasks by default; pass status (pending, in_progress, done, failed or all) for others; cancelled is reserved and nothing sets it yet. To resume after a crash, look for in_progress tasks first: a claim you were holding does not show as pending. Optionally filter to tasks having ALL of the given tags.

name: list
description: List live assets under a path (the directory and its whole subtree), one `slug  location` line each. Optionally filter to assets having ALL of the given tags; sort by name (default), created_at or updated_at; page with limit and offset.

name: read
description:
Read an asset by slug. With no flags it returns the raw content (default).
Request metadata fields individually with boolean flags — any combination of
name, path, content_type, kind, status, owner, tags, created_at, updated_at, backlinks,
created_by, updated_by, verified_by, version — and only those fields are returned.
Add content: true to include the body alongside the requested metadata. Pass
format: "json" for structured output (full asset when no flags; selected fields
when flags are set). Returns Not found for unknown or archived assets.

name: read_path
description:
Read an asset by location instead of slug. Provide either location (full path
including filename, e.g. "member/notes/plan.md") or path + name (directory + leaf).
Pass format: "json" for structured output. Optionally pass with: an array of fields
to return (content, name, path, content_type, kind, status, owner, tags, created_at,
updated_at, backlinks, created_by, updated_by, verified_by, version) — omit with for
raw content (text) or the full asset (json). Returns Not found for unknown or
archived assets.

name: remove_tag
description: Detach a tag from an asset by slug. The tag itself is not deleted even if it becomes orphaned.

name: restore
description: Restore a soft-deleted asset by slug. Conflict if a live asset now has its location.

name: search
description: Full-text + fuzzy-name search across live assets, optionally scoped to a path prefix and tag set. Filter by status (a note's open|done or a task's pending|in_progress|done|failed), by task_status (tasks only), or exclude assets having ANY of exclude_tags (e.g. tagged X but not done). Pass stale: true for assets whose stale_after review date has passed (false for the rest; assets with no review date are never stale). Optionally sort (name|created_at|updated_at) and paginate (limit/offset). Each result is a `slug  name  (dir)` line with a short content snippet around the first match beneath it. Pass include_versions: true to also match content an asset used to have but no longer does, for finding something you wrote and later edited away. Those hits are snippeted from the version and marked with the date it was displaced.

name: set_stale_after
description: Set the date after which an asset should be re-checked, without claiming it still holds. Use this when you know something needs revisiting by a date but have not re-read it; use `verify` when you have. Pass an empty stale_after to clear the review date. Find overdue assets with search(stale: true).

name: set_status
description: Set a lifecycle status ('open' or 'done') on a note, or clear it (omit/empty status). Not valid for tasks — those use claim_task, complete_task and fail_task.

name: tags
description: Enumerate the tags applied to live assets with a count of live assets per tag, sorted by count desc then name asc. Optionally scope to a path prefix with `within`.

name: update
description: Update an existing asset by slug. Snapshots prior content into versions on content change; an empty content clears it, omitting it leaves it alone. 'name', when renaming, is the leaf only (no whitespace, no '/', not '.' or '..') — it is not a path. Pass expected_version (from read's version field) to refuse the write with Conflict if someone else edited first. Not found if archived.

name: update_last_session
description: Overwrite your session checkpoint with where you are now: open threads, next step, anything the next session needs to resume without re-deriving it. Call this before finishing, and whenever you reach a milestone worth resuming from. Replaces the previous checkpoint (the old text is kept as a version). Each agent has its own checkpoint: pass agent when several agents share one token.

name: upsert
description: Create-or-update an asset by path + name. Updates the live asset at that path + name if one exists (snapshotting prior content), otherwise creates it. 'path' is the DIRECTORY only (no trailing filename or known file extension — those are rejected); 'name' is the leaf (no whitespace, no '/', not '.' or '..').

name: verify
description: Record that an asset's content still holds, and optionally set stale_after — the date after which it should be re-checked. Verification is not an edit: it leaves updated_at and version history alone. Pass an empty stale_after to clear the review date; omit it to leave it as is. Find overdue assets with search(stale: true).

name: versions
description: List prior versions of an asset by slug, newest first, with who wrote each.
